items.title: 5 Things to Eat This Weekend
items.text: Grub Street picks iara’s two cheesy breads: a cassava pão de queijo and a charcoal-grilled bun filled with garlic-cheese spread, made for sopping up the rest of the menu.

items.title: Off The Menu: Steak Houses on Parade
items.text: Florence Fabricant names iara among the week’s openings: an earthy room around a big open kitchen, with tuna and tapioca, cashew soup, cheese bread and picanha with cassava fries.

items.title: This New Restaurant Brings the Amazon Rainforest to the Lower East Side
items.text: Eater goes inside iara: how cassava changed Vitor’s life, a tucupi martini at the bar, and a 13-seat chef’s counter facing the open kitchen.

items.title: Iara Celebrates the Exquisite Abundance of the Amazon Rainforest
items.text: Vitor tells Resy how a trip to the Amazon after his father’s passing changed what he thought Brazilian food could be, from tingling jambu to tucupi hot sauce.

items.title: Iara
items.text: The Infatuation flags iara as one to know: red snapper moqueca, charcoal-grilled picanha and tapioca crisps with smoked trout mousse.

items.author: Douglas R.
items.text: Food: 10/10 Drinks: 10/10 Atmosphere: 10/10 Service: 10/10 Favorite dish: Moqueca The best new restaurant of 2026. Unique, thoughtfully designed, elegant but not stuffy, and incredibly welcoming. I can’t wait to go back!

items.author: D S
items.text: Incredible representation of Brazilian cuisine in Manhattan. Each course equally creative and humble to its roots. The fish, the picañha absolutely dialed in. Cocktails innovative while approachable. Can't wait to return!
items.pull: Incredible representation of Brazilian cuisine in Manhattan.

items.author: Krys J.
items.text: Who would have thought that food inspired by regions around the Amazon rainforest in Brazil would be this good 💯 was able to do an early preview tasting with chef Vitor and it was absolute 🔥!!

items.author: Kate J.
items.text:
It’s not often you go to a restaurant where every detail is thought out. The team at Iara did an exceptional job. The dishes and flatware are from
Brazil, the staff is trained on every unique ingredient (I even asked where the beans were from and they knew). The food is exceptional, with incredibly unique flavors clearly celebrating where they’re from. The menu is majority gluten free inherently, and as a previously gluten intolerant person this made my heart sing.

The staff was a delight, everyone was friendly, well trained and attentive. I cannot wait to come back for the next seasonal menu. Congratulations to this team this spot is phenomenal!
items.pull: Congratulations to this team this spot is phenomenal!
